help.intro: A scene of about two minutes in a German pharmacy: a customer has had a cough for two weeks and wants something strong, the pharmacist asks questions, explains the difference between prescription medicines and the ones you can simply buy, gives careful advice and in the end sends him to the doctor. The scene is invented; the rules it describes are real: in Germany you buy medicines only in a pharmacy, many need a prescription, and the pharmacy must advise you. You hear what you have just learnt: advice and suggestions with sollte and könnte (Sie sollten zum Arzt gehen. Sie könnten Tee trinken), and the health words (der Husten, die Erkältung, die Tablette, der Saft, das Rezept, die Nebenwirkung). Listen once for the whole scene, then once for each piece of advice.
help.tips[0].title: sollte and könnte: advice without an order
help.tips[0].text: sollte (should) gives advice: Sie sollten zum Arzt gehen. Du solltest mehr schlafen. könnte (could) makes a suggestion: Sie könnten einen Tee trinken. Wir könnten morgen anrufen. Both are softer than müssen (must) and the imperative. Forms: ich sollte / könnte, du solltest / könntest, er sollte / könnte, wir sollten / könnten, Sie sollten / könnten. The main verb stays at the end in the infinitive. Other soft forms: An Ihrer Stelle würde ich … (in your place I would), Es wäre gut, wenn … (it would be good if).
help.tips[0].examples[0].en: You should take this seriously and go to the doctor. Until then you could take a cough syrup.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: In your place I would not work any more today.
help.tips[0].check.q: Advice, polite: 'You should drink more water.'
help.tips[0].check.why: sollte is the soft advice form; müssen and the imperative are stronger.
help.tips[1].title: Words at the pharmacy
help.tips[1].text: die Apotheke (pharmacy, the only place for medicines), das Medikament (medicine), die Tablette, der Saft (syrup), die Tropfen (drops), die Salbe (ointment), das Rezept (prescription: rezeptpflichtig = prescription only, rezeptfrei = over the counter), die Nebenwirkung (side effect), die Packungsbeilage (leaflet), der Husten (cough), der Schnupfen (cold, runny nose), die Erkältung, das Fieber, die Halsschmerzen. Verbs: einnehmen (to take a medicine), wirken (to work, take effect), verschreiben (to prescribe).
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: This medicine is prescription only; for that you have to go to the doctor. The cough syrup is over the counter.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: Take the syrup three times a day. Read the leaflet because of the side effects.
help.tips[1].check.options[0]: you can buy it without a prescription
help.tips[1].check.answer: you can buy it without a prescription
help.tips[1].check.why: rezeptfrei = free of prescription, over the counter.
help.remember[0]: Sie sollten … (advice), Sie könnten … (suggestion), An Ihrer Stelle würde ich …; verb at the end.
help.remember[1]: rezeptpflichtig / rezeptfrei, Nebenwirkung, Packungsbeilage, einnehmen, Husten, Erkältung.
help.exam: Short scenes at a pharmacy or doctor's with advice and recommendations are a typical listening task at this level.
help.hook: Two weeks of coughing, a wish for something strong, and a pharmacist who says: you should take this seriously. Listen to the advice.
help.vocab[4].example: Trinken Sie warmen Tee mit Honig.
passageTranslation:
Pharmacist: Good day, what can I do for you?
Customer: Good day. I need something for a cough. Something strong, please.
Pharmacist: Since when have you had the cough?
Customer: For two weeks. First I had a cold, that has gone, but the cough stays. Especially at night.
Pharmacist: Two weeks is long. Do you have a fever?
Customer: No. But I am tired, and my throat hurts from coughing.
Pharmacist: I will gladly give you a cough syrup, that is over the counter. But honestly: you should take this seriously. Two weeks of coughing without fever, a doctor should listen to that.
Customer: I have no time for the doctor. Do you not have something stronger?
Pharmacist: The strong medicines are prescription only. I may not sell them without a prescription, even if I wanted to. That is the law.
Customer: Hm. And what can I do until then?
Pharmacist: You could take this syrup, one spoon three times a day. It calms the cough, especially at night. You should drink a lot, warm tea with honey. And you could open the bedroom window in the evening; dry air makes the cough worse.
Customer: Does the syrup have side effects?
Pharmacist: It can make you tired. That is why you should not drive after the syrup. Everything else is in the leaflet. Please read it.
Customer: Good. What does it cost?
Pharmacist: Eight euros ninety. And one more thing: in your place I would call the doctor tomorrow morning. At eight o'clock, that is when you most likely get an appointment.
Customer: Okay, you win. I will call tomorrow.
Pharmacist: Get well soon!
questions[0].explanation: "Seit zwei Wochen. Zuerst hatte ich eine Erkältung, die ist weg, aber der Husten bleibt."
questions[0].questionTranslation: Since when has the customer had a cough?
questions[1].explanation: sollte + infinitive is the soft advice form, weaker than müssen or an imperative.
questions[1].questionTranslation: 'You should take this seriously.' What is that?
questions[1].optionsTranslation[0]: a strict order from the pharmacist
questions[2].options[3]: weil der Husten nicht schlimm ist
questions[2].explanation: "Die starken Medikamente sind rezeptpflichtig. Die darf ich ohne Rezept nicht verkaufen … Das ist Gesetz."
questions[2].questionTranslation: Why does the pharmacist not sell a strong medicine?
questions[2].optionsTranslation[1]: because strong medicines are prescription only and she must obey the law
questions[2].optionsTranslation[2]: because the customer does not have enough money for a strong medicine
questions[2].optionsTranslation[3]: because the cough is not bad
questions[3].explanation: "Sie könnten diesen Saft nehmen, dreimal täglich einen Löffel."
questions[3].questionTranslation: How often should the customer take the syrup?
questions[3].optionsTranslation[1]: one spoon three times a day
questions[3].optionsTranslation[2]: only at night, directly before sleeping
questions[4].options[0]: das Fenster öffnen, weil trockene Luft den Husten schlimmer macht
questions[4].options[3]: die Heizung aufdrehen, weil es kalt ist
questions[4].explanation: "Und Sie könnten abends das Fenster im Schlafzimmer öffnen; trockene Luft macht den Husten schlimmer."
questions[4].questionTranslation: What could the customer do in the evening, and why?
questions[4].optionsTranslation[0]: open the window, because dry air makes the cough worse
questions[4].optionsTranslation[1]: do sport, because exercise is healthy and drives the cough away
questions[4].optionsTranslation[2]: drink coffee, because he is tired
questions[4].optionsTranslation[3]: turn up the heating, because it is cold
questions[5].explanation: "Er kann müde machen. Deshalb sollten Sie nach dem Saft nicht Auto fahren."
questions[5].questionTranslation: What side effect does the syrup have, and what follows from it?
questions[5].optionsTranslation[0]: It causes fever; you should stay in bed and sleep a lot.
questions[5].optionsTranslation[1]: It makes you tired; you should not drive afterwards.
questions[5].optionsTranslation[2]: It makes you hungry; you should eat a lot.
questions[6].explanation: An Ihrer Stelle würde ich … = in your place I would …: a polite way of giving advice.
questions[6].questionTranslation: 'In your place I would call the doctor tomorrow morning.' What does that mean?
questions[6].optionsTranslation[0]: The pharmacist herself calls the doctor tomorrow morning and makes an appointment.
questions[6].optionsTranslation[1]: The pharmacist advises: if I were you, I would call the doctor.
questions[6].optionsTranslation[2]: The customer must go to the doctor immediately.
questions[7].explanation: "Okay, Sie haben gewonnen. Ich rufe morgen an." He buys the syrup for 8.90 and will call the doctor.
questions[7].questionTranslation: What does the customer do in the end?
questions[7].optionsTranslation[1]: He goes home without syrup because he has no prescription.
questions[7].optionsTranslation[2]: He takes the syrup and will call the doctor tomorrow.
questions[7].optionsTranslation[3]: He goes to the doctor immediately.
questions[2].options[1]: weil starke Medikamente rezeptpflichtig sind und sie das Gesetz einhalten muss
